rule: TRACED nodes require a source. PROPOSED/UNKNOWN nodes carry no confidence. CONTESTED nodes preserve all accounts.

nodes.claim: Record: hexagonal_cell_efficiency = 0.97, 'ratio of honey volume stored per unit wax mass ... vs next-best regular tessellation'
Any partition of the plane into regions of equal area has perimeter at least that of the regular hexagonal tiling (2D).
nodes.note: Published Discrete Comput Geom 25:1-22 (2001); repo cites '36:5-69 (1999)' -> CITATION_MISMATCH. Theorem is 2D perimeter; record claims 3D volume per wax mass -> SCOPE_MISMATCH.

nodes.claim: The 3D bee cell (three-rhombus base) is not surface-minimizing; two hexagons + two rhombi is more economical, saving <0.35% of the opening area.
nodes.note: With non-zero wall thickness the three-rhombus base may be closer to optimum (Weaire & Phelan, as reported in Apidologie 2022). Optimality in 3D is regime-dependent on wall thickness.

nodes.claim: Wall thickness: zero (idealized) vs real non-uniform beeswax walls.
Cells are built circular; visco-elastic wax heated by workers flows near triple junctions; surface-energy minimization straightens walls into rounded hexagons.
nodes.note: Three accounts preserved, not reconciled: (a) surface-tension wax flow (Karihaloo 2013); (b) thermal expansion and stress above yield under a temperature gradient, without melting (Talukdar & Dutta, SN Appl Sci 2019); (c) workers iteratively equalising angular space at junctions, self-organised (npj/Nature 2026). Divergence is retained as data.

nodes.claim: Wax flows visco-elastically at about 45 °C at the triple junction.
Beeswax melts at 62–64 °C (upper regime bound: comb structure fails).
Brood nest regulated at 33–36 °C; capped brood 34.8–35.9 °C across ambient 13–41 °C.
Derived operating regime for hexagon formation: local wax ~45 °C, nest ~33–36 °C, below melt 62–64 °C.
nodes.note: Lower bound 45 °C is 'about'; treat as CONDITIONAL until a source gives a range.

nodes.claim: Beeswax composition: monoesters 35–45%, hydrocarbons 12–16%, free fatty acids 12–14%; hydrocarbons probably from oenocytes.
Secreted as liquid by four pairs of wax glands on young workers; glands largest ~day 12, decline after day 18; ~1 million scales per kg.
Wax is synthesised from sugar: ~8 kg honey consumed per kg wax.

value.deviation: sources span 6.66–8.80 (Whitcomb 1946, via Wikipedia) to 8–15 (FAO T0104E)

nodes.claim: Heat for wax working and brood comes from worker thoracic muscle metabolism fuelled by nectar sugar; ~40% of the colony's annual energy intake goes to brood-nest heating.
Nectar sugars originate from sucrose loaded from phloem, produced by photosynthesis.
Total solar irradiance at 1 AU: 1360.8 ± 0.5 W/m² (2008 solar minimum).
nodes.note: GAP: no repository entity represents incoming solar radiation. SOLAR_WIND is a plasma flow.

nodes.claim: Open, far-from-equilibrium systems maintain ordered structure only through continuous energy/matter exchange and disappear if it ceases (dissipative structures).
nodes.note: Energy conservation is assumed as the accounting law for the chain; no repository equation reference exists for it.
Which repository plant entities stand for nectar sources is an owner decision.

nodes.claim: Workers heat the wax with their bodies during comb building.

cycles.name: circle→hexagon transition
cycles.period_text: ≈6 s fully heated; ≈36 s partially heated
cycles.note: A relaxation, not a repeat. Recorded as a transient phase inside the comb-building cycle; whether it counts as a cycle in its own right is an owner call.

cycles.name: daily activity (circadian)
cycles.note: Nesting position is assumed; a honeybee circadian source has not been attached.

cycles.name: wax-gland age window
cycles.period_text: begins <1 wk, peaks ≈2 wk (≈day 12), declines after day 18
cycles.context: worker life stage; swarm regime overrides (all ages build)

cycles.name: colony annual cycle
cycles.period_text: 1 year (winter cluster vs summer energy partition)
